title: They Look Good… But Do They Love Like Christ?
paragraphs:
They Look Good… But Do They Love Like Christ?
The Green Flags That Heaven Notices (And Your Soul Can’t Afford to Ignore)
You almost chose them because of how they looked.

The smile. The confidence. The way they carried themselves like they had everything together. And if you’re honest… part of you wanted to be chosen by someone like that, because it felt like it would finally prove something about you.
But somewhere deep inside, past the attraction and the excitement, there was a quiet voice asking a question you didn’t want to face:
“Will this lead me closer to Christ… or slowly pull me away?”
Because not everything that shines is sent from God.
And not everything that feels right… is right.

The world taught you to look for beauty, status, chemistry, and attention. But heaven looks for something else entirely. Scripture doesn’t celebrate what impresses the eyes… it reveals what transforms the soul.
In 1 Samuel 16:7, when the prophet was about to choose a king based on appearance, God interrupted him with something that still shakes every shallow standard we carry today:

“כִּי הָאָדָם יִרְאֶה לַעֵינַיִם וַיהוָה יִרְאֶה לַלֵּבָב”
(ki ha’adam yir’eh la’einayim, v’Adonai yir’eh la’levav)
“For man looks at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart.”
The heart.
Not their style. Not their charm. Not their following. Not how they make you feel in the moment.
Their heart.
Because what lives in their heart… will eventually live in your life.
And this is where most people miss it.
They chase attraction, but ignore alignment. They fall for energy, but ignore evidence. They celebrate attention, but overlook intention.
But the real green flags? The ones that matter more than looks?
They’re quieter. Deeper. Sometimes even uncomfortable… because they don’t just attract you, they expose you.
A person who fears God more than losing you.
That’s rare.
Proverbs 9:10 says, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.”
The Hebrew word for fear here is “יִרְאָה” (yirah), which isn’t terror… it’s reverence. Awe. A deep awareness of God that shapes decisions when nobody is watching.
When someone carries that kind of reverence, they won’t play with your heart casually. They won’t flirt with sin and call it love. They won’t lead you somewhere they know God would not go.
They won’t just want you.
They’ll want to honor God with you.
And that changes everything.
Another green flag the world ignores?
Conviction.
Not perfection. Not performance. Conviction.
The kind that makes someone pause mid-conversation and say, “That didn’t sit right with me.”
The kind that leads them to repent, not defend.
In John 16:8, Jesus speaks of the Holy Spirit:

“ἐλέγξει τὸν κόσμον περὶ ἁμαρτίας”
(elegxei ton kosmon peri hamartias)
“He will convict the world concerning sin.”
Conviction is not condemnation. It’s evidence that God is still speaking.
When someone can be corrected without becoming defensive… when they can admit wrong without shifting blame… when they choose growth over ego… that’s not weakness.
That’s a soul being shaped by Christ.
And that kind of person won’t destroy you when things get hard.
They’ll grow with you.
Another green flag?
They protect purity… even when it costs them something.
Not just physical boundaries, but emotional and spiritual ones too.
1 Thessalonians 4:3 says, “For this is the will of God, your sanctification…”
The Greek word for sanctification is “ἁγιασμός” (hagiasmos), meaning to be set apart.
A person who values being set apart won’t rush intimacy just to keep you. They won’t pressure you into compromise. They won’t trade holiness for temporary pleasure.
They understand something the world refuses to accept:
Love that dishonors God… will eventually dishonor you.
And maybe this is the one that hits the deepest…
They lead you closer to Jesus, not further from Him.
Not just with words. With their life.
With how they speak. How they respond under pressure. How they handle conflict. How they treat people who can’t benefit them.
Because anyone can quote Scripture.
But not everyone lives it.
James 1:22 warns, “Be doers of the word, and not hearers only…”
The Greek says, “γίνεσθε δὲ ποιηταὶ λόγου” (ginesthe de poiētai logou)
Become doers.
Not performers.
Not pretenders.
Doers.
If someone’s presence in your life is making you pray less, compromise more, question your convictions, and slowly drift away from God… that is not love.
No matter how good it feels.
Because real love… draws you into truth, not away from it.
And here’s the part nobody says out loud:
You can be deeply attracted to someone who is spiritually dangerous for you.
And you can overlook someone who carries the very peace you’ve been praying for… because they don’t fit your “type.”
But your “type” never saved you.
Jesus did.
And if your relationship doesn’t reflect Him… it will eventually reveal what it’s missing.
This is where everything shifts.
Because the question is no longer, “Do they like me?”
It becomes:
“Do they reflect Christ?”
Because if they don’t… you’re not just risking your heart.
You’re risking your direction.
Your peace.
Your calling.
Your eternity.
And maybe you’re reading this right now, realizing something you didn’t want to admit.
That you’ve been settling for attention instead of alignment.
That you’ve been choosing what looks good… over what is God.
That you’ve ignored red flags because you were desperate to feel loved.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
You’re not alone in this.
But you don’t have to stay here.
Because the Gospel was never about perfect people choosing perfectly.
It’s about broken people being rewritten by grace.
Romans 5:8 reminds us:
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
He didn’t wait for you to choose right.
He came to make you right.
And when Jesus enters your life… He doesn’t just change who you are.
He changes what you’re willing to accept.
So now you don’t just want love.
You want God-honoring love.
You don’t just want connection.
You want covenant.
You don’t just want someone who looks good beside you.
You want someone who walks with Christ beside you.
Someone you love needs this reminder too.
And if you’re serious about growing deeper in Jesus Christ, about healing, about discernment, about walking in truth instead of confusion… take the next step.
Because glorifying God isn’t passive.
It’s intentional.
And sometimes… it looks like supporting the very truth that is helping set people free.
So don’t just feel convicted.
Respond.
Because the kind of love you choose… will shape the life you live.
And the wrong one doesn’t just break your heart.
It slowly silences your relationship with God.
And that’s a cost your soul was never meant to carry.
